Edit fields like prefix. id is a composite key '{addressId}*!{carrierCode}*!{poolPointAddressId}' URL-encoded. Record carries a 'version' field that increments on every successful write (observed 1 -> 2 -> 3 across edit + revert) -- looks like optimistic-locking support, but whether a stale/mismatched version is REJECTED was not tested (edge case matrix row 12 in KNOWLEDGE-BASE.md). Strip the nested carrierInfo object before PUT, it is a read-only expansion. VERSION FIELD IS NOT OPTIMISTIC LOCKING (settled live 2026-08-11): PUT with a deliberately stale version (sent 1 while the stored record was at 2) was ACCEPTED -- 200, the change applied, version bumped to 3. No 409, no error. So `version` is a write counter only and this API offers NO lost-update protection: two workers editing the same record silently clobber each other. Any concurrent executor must serialise per-record itself.
